gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Nippo has small letters that stand nearly as tall as its capitals, cut like bent wire and unmistakably technical. And Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart, so it earns its place by staying open while Nippo does the shouting in big, short lines.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoined: Nippo draws its wire-cut letters with lines that hold their thickness, nearly capital-tall even in lowercase. And Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined answers with roomy gaps between curve ends and stems, so the two share a modern, uncluttered footing on the page.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hier: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs reads tall and outward-pointing, its x-height rising close to cap height like a plain sans in a hurry. And Nippo matches that stature with wire-cut lowercase and a stylus-steady stroke, which is where the pair really lands.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Contemporary and a bit technical, Nippo looks bent from wire. Noto Sans Arabic sits beneath it with wide openings and a pronounced x-height, a soft-spoken sans against the heading's drawn-wire stiffness, and that gap in temperament is the pair's best quality.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian is approachable, with tall, full s and z shapes and rounds that open inviting. Nippo handles the loud work with diagonals as thick as its uprights, while Noto Sans Armenian handles the quiet, friendly work of carrying the text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Noto Sans Avestan reads modern and clean, its curve tips stopping short of touching and its x-height pronounced. Nippo, drawn with pencil-like lines, earns its keep big and brief.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Nippo is wire-cut and technical, with diagonals as heavy as its verticals. Noto Sans Balinese follows with breathing space inside each curve and short ascenders, so a long page of it would read smoothly and stay easy on the eye.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads open and modern, with big counters in every small letter. Nippo does flat, single-weight linework that holds up as a heading, while Noto Sans Bamum lets text breathe on the page.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Nippo's small letters stand nearly as tall as its capitals, drawn in a steady, unshaded outline. And Noto Sans Bassa Vah, with its dominant midsection and pliers-like c, would carry a long stretch of text with a sturdy, confident feel.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-batak: Stubby, upright and sturdy: Noto Sans Batak has a towering x-height and a wide e that never squeezes shut. Nippo, bent from a single length of wire, is the one to give big, short lines.
